name: 024_trend_regime_both_tf5
hypothesis: R3.1 asks whether a long-or-flat trend regime is a calmer way to hold BTC. This asks the other half of the same question and it is the one that decides whether the family is worth more than a smoother ride: when the regime is DOWN, is the right answer to be flat, or to be short? The counterparty for a short in a down-regime is the long crowd that has not yet capitulated, and the cost of being wrong is a whipsaw back through a 200-bar EMA. Buy & hold's 2022 was -64% and a rule that was short for even part of that would beat it outright; a rule whose short leg loses money is not a regime rule, it is a long rule with a fee, which is why the kill condition here is written on the short leg's own gross_r and not on the combined mean R. [Timeframe variant of 024_trend_regime_both, 60m -> 5m, mode chart: same bar counts and ATR multiples, hold x0.0833333, pct stop x0.289.]
